passages.text: Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had resided, the land of Canaan.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was a son of Isaac.
Isaac was his father.
Jacob lived in the land of Canaan.
Canaan was the land where Isaac had lived before.
Jacob stayed in the same land as his father.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מְגוּרֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃

passages.text: This is the account of Jacob. When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers, the sons of his father’s wives Bilhah and Zilpah, and he brought their father a bad report about them.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the son of Isaac and the grandson of Abraham.
Jacob lived in the land of Canaan.
This is the account of Jacob’s family.
Joseph was Jacob’s son.
Joseph was seventeen years old.
Joseph took care of the flock with his brothers.
Joseph’s brothers were the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah.
Bilhah and Zilpah were Jacob’s wives.
Joseph brought a bad report about his brothers to their father.
passages.original: אֵ֣לֶּה׀ תֹּלְד֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֗ב יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן־ שְׁבַֽע־ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת־ אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־ דִּבָּתָ֥ם רָעָ֖ה אֶל־ אֲבִיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons, because Joseph had been born to him in his old age; so he made him a robe of many colors.
passages.sermon:
Israel was also called Jacob.
Israel had many sons.
Joseph was one of his sons.
Joseph was born when Israel was old.
Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons.
Israel made a special robe for Joseph.
The robe had many colors.
passages.original: וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אָהַ֤ב אֶת־ יוֹסֵף֙ מִכָּל־ בָּנָ֔יו כִּֽי־ בֶן־ זְקֻנִ֥ים ה֖וּא ל֑וֹ וְעָ֥שָׂה ל֖וֹ כְּתֹ֥נֶת פַּסִּֽים׃

passages.text: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was one of Jacob’s sons.
Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons.
Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved Joseph most.
Joseph’s brothers hated Joseph.
Joseph’s brothers could not speak kindly to Joseph.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֣וּ אֶחָ֗יו כִּֽי־ אֹת֞וֹ אָהַ֤ב אֲבִיהֶם֙ מִכָּל־ אֶחָ֔יו וַֽיִּשְׂנְא֖וּ אֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ דַּבְּר֥וֹ לְשָׁלֹֽם׃

passages.text: Then Joseph had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Israel.
Israel loved Joseph more than his other sons.
Joseph had a dream.
Joseph told his dream to his brothers.
His brothers already hated him.
After he told them the dream, they hated him even more.
passages.original: וַיַּחֲלֹ֤ם יוֹסֵף֙ חֲל֔וֹם וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיּוֹסִ֥פוּ ע֖וֹד שְׂנֹ֥א אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He said to them, “Listen to this dream I had: We were binding sheaves of grain in the field, and suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons.
Joseph’s brothers hated him because of this.
Joseph spoke to his brothers.
Joseph said, “Listen to the dream I had.”
He said, “We were in the field.”
He said, “We were binding sheaves of grain.”
He said, “My sheaf stood up.”
He said, “Your sheaves gathered around my sheaf.”
He said, “Your sheaves bowed down to my sheaf.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם שִׁמְעוּ־ נָ֕א הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָלָֽמְתִּי׃ וְ֠הִנֵּה אֲנַ֜חְנוּ מְאַלְּמִ֤ים אֲלֻמִּים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה קָ֥מָה אֲלֻמָּתִ֖י וְגַם־ נִצָּ֑בָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה תְסֻבֶּ֙ינָה֙ אֲלֻמֹּ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וַתִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖יןָ לַאֲלֻמָּתִֽי׃

passages.text: “Do you intend to reign over us?” his brothers asked. “Will you actually rule us?” So they hated him even more because of his dream and his statements.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph had brothers.
Joseph told his brothers about his dream.
His brothers spoke to Joseph.
They asked Joseph, “Do you intend to reign over us?”
They also asked, “Will you actually rule us?”
His brothers hated Joseph even more.
They hated him because of his dreams.
They hated him because of his words.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ אֶחָ֔יו הֲמָלֹ֤ךְ תִּמְלֹךְ֙ עָלֵ֔ינוּ אִם־ מָשׁ֥וֹל תִּמְשֹׁ֖ל בָּ֑נוּ וַיּוֹסִ֤פוּ עוֹד֙ שְׂנֹ֣א אֹת֔וֹ עַל־ חֲלֹמֹתָ֖יו וְעַל־ דְּבָרָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Joseph had another dream and told it to his brothers. “Look,” he said, “I had another dream, and this time the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph had a special gift from God.
Joseph could understand dreams.
Joseph had another dream.
Joseph told this dream to his brothers.
Joseph said, “Look, I had another dream.”
In this dream, the sun was bowing down to me.
The moon was bowing down to me.
Eleven stars were bowing down to me.
passages.original: וַיַּחֲלֹ֥ם עוֹד֙ חֲל֣וֹם אַחֵ֔ר וַיְסַפֵּ֥ר אֹת֖וֹ לְאֶחָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֨ה חָלַ֤מְתִּֽי חֲלוֹם֙ ע֔וֹד וְהִנֵּ֧ה הַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ וְהַיָּרֵ֗חַ וְאַחַ֤ד עָשָׂר֙ כּֽוֹכָבִ֔ים מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֖ים לִֽי׃

passages.text: He told his father and brothers, but his father rebuked him and said, “What is this dream that you have had? Will your mother and brothers and I actually come and bow down to the ground before you?”
passages.sermon:
Joseph told his father and his brothers about his dream.
His father rebuked him.
His father said, “What is this dream you have had?”
His father asked, “Will I, your mother, and your brothers really come and bow down to you on the ground?”
passages.original: וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר אֶל־ אָבִיו֮ וְאֶל־ אֶחָיו֒ וַיִּגְעַר־ בּ֣וֹ אָבִ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָ֛ה הַחֲל֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָלָ֑מְתָּ הֲב֣וֹא נָב֗וֹא אֲנִי֙ וְאִמְּךָ֣ וְאַחֶ֔יךָ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֥ת לְךָ֖ אָֽרְצָה׃

passages.text: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept in mind what he had said.
passages.sermon: Joseph’s brothers felt jealous of him.\r\nJoseph’s father remembered what Joseph said.
passages.original: וַיְקַנְאוּ־ ב֖וֹ אֶחָ֑יו וְאָבִ֖יו שָׁמַ֥ר אֶת־ הַדָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: Some time later, Joseph’s brothers had gone to pasture their father’s flocks near Shechem.
passages.sermon:
Joseph had brothers.
Their father was Jacob, also called Israel.
Joseph’s brothers took their father’s flocks.
They went to Shechem.
They pastured the flocks there.
passages.original: וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אֶחָ֑יו לִרְע֛וֹת אֶׄתׄ־ צֹ֥אן אֲבִיהֶ֖ם בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Israel said to him, “Are not your brothers pasturing the flocks at Shechem? Get ready; I am sending you to them.” “I am ready,” Joseph replied.
passages.sermon:
Israel was Joseph’s father.
Israel spoke to Joseph.
Israel said, “Your brothers are pasturing the flocks at Shechem.”
Israel said, “Go. I will send you to them.”
Joseph replied, “I am ready.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ רֹעִ֣ים בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם לְכָ֖ה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ הִנֵּֽנִי׃

passages.text: Then Israel told him, “Go now and see how your brothers and the flocks are faring, and bring word back to me.” So he sent him off from the Valley of Hebron. And when Joseph arrived in Shechem, a man found him wandering in the field and asked, “What are you looking for?”
passages.sermon:
Israel was Joseph’s father.
Israel spoke to Joseph.
Israel said, “Go now.
See how your brothers are doing.
See how the flocks are doing.
Bring word back to me.”
Israel sent Joseph from the Valley of Hebron.
Joseph came to Shechem.
A man found Joseph in the field.
Joseph was wandering in the field.
The man asked Joseph, “What are you looking for?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ לֶךְ־ נָ֨א רְאֵ֜ה אֶת־ שְׁל֤וֹם אַחֶ֙יךָ֙ וְאֶת־ שְׁל֣וֹם הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֵ֖נִי דָּבָ֑ר וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֙הוּ֙ מֵעֵ֣מֶק חֶבְר֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖א שְׁכֶֽמָה׃ וַיִּמְצָאֵ֣הוּ אִ֔ישׁ וְהִנֵּ֥ה תֹעֶ֖ה בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיִּשְׁאָלֵ֧הוּ הָאִ֛ישׁ לֵאמֹ֖ר מַה־ תְּבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

passages.text: “I am looking for my brothers,” Joseph replied. “Can you please tell me where they are pasturing their flocks?”
passages.sermon: Joseph spoke to the man.\r\nJoseph said, “I am looking for my brothers.”\r\nJoseph asked, “Please tell me where they are pasturing their flocks.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֶת־ אַחַ֖י אָנֹכִ֣י מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ הַגִּֽידָה־ נָּ֣א לִ֔י אֵיפֹ֖ה הֵ֥ם רֹעִֽים׃

passages.text: “They have moved on from here,” the man answered. “I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’ ” So Joseph set out after his brothers and found them at Dothan.
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to Joseph.
The man said, “Your brothers have left this place.”
The man said, “I heard them say, ‘Let us go to Dothan.’”
Joseph went to look for his brothers.
Joseph found his brothers in Dothan.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הָאִישׁ֙ נָסְע֣וּ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֤י שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֹֽמְרִ֔ים נֵלְכָ֖ה דֹּתָ֑יְנָה וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יוֹסֵף֙ אַחַ֣ר אֶחָ֔יו וַיִּמְצָאֵ֖ם בְּדֹתָֽן׃

passages.text: Now Joseph’s brothers saw him in the distance, and before he arrived, they plotted to kill him.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers saw Joseph from far away.
Joseph had not yet reached them.
Joseph’s brothers made a plan.
They planned to kill Joseph.
passages.original: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מֵרָחֹ֑ק וּבְטֶ֙רֶם֙ יִקְרַ֣ב אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּֽתְנַכְּל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ לַהֲמִיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers saw Joseph coming.
Joseph’s brothers spoke to each other.
They said, “Here comes that dreamer.”
Joseph was known for his dreams.
Joseph’s dreams made his brothers angry.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ אָחִ֑יו הִנֵּ֗ה בַּ֛עַל הַחֲלֹמ֥וֹת הַלָּזֶ֖ה בָּֽא׃

passages.text: “Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits. We can say that a vicious animal has devoured him. Then we shall see what becomes of his dreams!”
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers hated him.
They saw Joseph coming from a distance.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “Come now, let us kill him.”
They planned to throw Joseph into one of the pits.
They said, “We can say a wild animal has eaten him.”
They wanted to see what would happen to Joseph’s dreams.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ לְכ֣וּ וְנַֽהַרְגֵ֗הוּ וְנַשְׁלִכֵ֙הוּ֙ בְּאַחַ֣ד הַבֹּר֔וֹת וְאָמַ֕רְנוּ חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ וְנִרְאֶ֕ה מַה־ יִּהְי֖וּ חֲלֹמֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: When Reuben heard this, he tried to rescue Joseph from their hands. “Let us not take his life,” he said.
passages.sermon:
Reuben was Joseph’s oldest brother.
Reuben heard his brothers’ plan to kill Joseph.
Reuben tried to rescue Joseph from his brothers.
Reuben said, “Let us not take his life.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע רְאוּבֵ֔ן וַיַּצִּלֵ֖הוּ מִיָּדָ֑ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹ֥א נַכֶּ֖נּוּ נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: “Do not shed his blood. Throw him into this pit in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him.” Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.
passages.sermon:
Reuben was Joseph’s oldest brother.
Reuben spoke to his brothers.
He said, “Do not shed his blood.”
He said, “Throw him into this pit in the wilderness.”
He said, “Do not lay a hand on him.”
Reuben said this to save Joseph from his brothers.
Reuben wanted to rescue Joseph from them.
Reuben wanted to return Joseph to his father.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֣ם׀ רְאוּבֵן֮ אַל־ תִּשְׁפְּכוּ־ דָם֒ הַשְׁלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֗וֹ אֶל־ הַבּ֤וֹר הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְיָ֖ד אַל־ תִּשְׁלְחוּ־ ב֑וֹ לְמַ֗עַן הַצִּ֤יל אֹתוֹ֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם לַהֲשִׁיב֖וֹ אֶל־ אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the robe of many colors he was wearing— and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph had many brothers.
Joseph wore a special robe of many colors.
Joseph came to his brothers.
His brothers saw him.
His brothers took Joseph’s robe from him.
They removed the robe of many colors that Joseph was wearing.
His brothers seized Joseph.
They threw Joseph into a pit.
The pit was empty.
There was no water in the pit.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִ֕י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א יוֹסֵ֖ף אֶל־ אֶחָ֑יו וַיַּפְשִׁ֤יטוּ אֶת־ יוֹסֵף֙ אֶת־ כֻּתָּנְתּ֔וֹ אֶת־ כְּתֹ֥נֶת הַפַּסִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃ וַיִּ֨קָּחֻ֔הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֥כוּ אֹת֖וֹ הַבֹּ֑רָה וְהַבּ֣וֹר רֵ֔ק אֵ֥ין בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And as they sat down to eat a meal, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers sat down to eat a meal.
They looked up.
They saw a caravan.
The caravan belonged to Ishmaelites.
The Ishmaelites were coming from Gilead.
Their camels carried spices.
Their camels carried balm.
Their camels carried myrrh.
The Ishmaelites were traveling to Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֵּשְׁבוּ֮ לֶֽאֱכָל־ לֶחֶם֒ וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיהֶם֙ וַיִּרְא֔וּ וְהִנֵּה֙ אֹרְחַ֣ת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים בָּאָ֖ה מִגִּלְעָ֑ד וּגְמַלֵּיהֶ֣ם נֹֽשְׂאִ֗ים נְכֹאת֙ וּצְרִ֣י וָלֹ֔ט הוֹלְכִ֖ים לְהוֹרִ֥יד מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

passages.text: Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?
passages.sermon:
Judah spoke to his brothers.
Judah asked a question.
Judah said, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother?
What profit will we gain if we cover up his blood?”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶל־ אֶחָ֑יו מַה־ בֶּ֗צַע כִּ֤י נַהֲרֹג֙ אֶת־ אָחִ֔ינוּ וְכִסִּ֖ינוּ אֶת־ דָּמֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Come, let us sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay a hand on him; for he is our brother, our own flesh.” And they agreed.
passages.sermon:
Judah spoke to his brothers.
Judah said, "Let us sell Joseph to the Ishmaelites."
Judah said, "Let us not harm Joseph."
Judah said, "Joseph is our brother."
Judah said, "Joseph is our own flesh."
The brothers listened to Judah.
The brothers agreed with Judah.
passages.original: לְכ֞וּ וְנִמְכְּרֶ֣נּוּ לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֗ים וְיָדֵ֙נוּ֙ אַל־ תְּהִי־ ב֔וֹ כִּֽי־ אָחִ֥ינוּ בְשָׂרֵ֖נוּ ה֑וּא וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֖וּ אֶחָֽיו׃

passages.text: So when the Midianite traders passed by, his brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the son of Jacob.
Joseph’s brothers hated him.
Midianite traders passed by.
Joseph’s brothers saw the traders.
Joseph’s brothers pulled Joseph out of the pit.
Joseph’s brothers sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites.
They sold Joseph for twenty pieces of silver.
The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ֩ אֲנָשִׁ֨ים מִדְיָנִ֜ים סֹֽחֲרִ֗ים וַֽיִּמְשְׁכוּ֙ וַיַּֽעֲל֤וּ אֶת־ יוֹסֵף֙ מִן־ הַבּ֔וֹר וַיִּמְכְּר֧וּ אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֛ף לַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וַיָּבִ֥יאוּ אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֖ף מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃

passages.text: When Reuben returned to the pit and saw that Joseph was not there, he tore his clothes, returned to his brothers, and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
passages.sermon:
Reuben was Joseph’s older brother.
Reuben returned to the pit.
He looked into the pit.
Joseph was not in the pit.
Reuben saw that Joseph was gone.
Reuben tore his clothes.
He went back to his brothers.
He spoke to his brothers.
He said, “The boy is gone.”
He said, “What am I going to do?”
passages.original: וַיָּ֤שָׁב רְאוּבֵן֙ אֶל־ הַבּ֔וֹר וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵין־ יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבּ֑וֹר וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת־ בְּגָדָֽיו׃ וַיָּ֥שָׁב אֶל־ אֶחָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר הַיֶּ֣לֶד אֵינֶ֔נּוּ וַאֲנִ֖י אָ֥נָה אֲנִי־ בָֽא׃

passages.text: Then they took Joseph’s robe, slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.
passages.sermon: Joseph’s brothers took Joseph’s robe.\r\nThey killed a young goat.\r\nThey dipped Joseph’s robe in the goat’s blood.
passages.original: וַיִּקְח֖וּ אֶת־ כְּתֹ֣נֶת יוֹסֵ֑ף וַֽיִּשְׁחֲטוּ֙ שְׂעִ֣יר עִזִּ֔ים וַיִּטְבְּל֥וּ אֶת־ הַכֻּתֹּ֖נֶת בַּדָּֽם׃

passages.text: They sent the robe of many colors to their father and said, “We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son’s robe or not.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph’s brothers took his robe of many colors.
They sent the robe to their father Jacob.
They brought the robe to Jacob.
They spoke to Jacob.
They said, “We found this robe.”
They said, “Please look at it.”
They said, “See if this is your son’s robe or not.”
passages.original: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֞וּ אֶת־ כְּתֹ֣נֶת הַפַּסִּ֗ים וַיָּבִ֙יאוּ֙ אֶל־ אֲבִיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ זֹ֣את מָצָ֑אנוּ הַכֶּר־ נָ֗א הַכְּתֹ֧נֶת בִּנְךָ֛ הִ֖וא אִם־ לֹֽא׃

passages.text: His father recognized it and said, “It is my son’s robe! A vicious animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!”
passages.sermon:
Jacob was Joseph’s father.
Jacob saw the robe.
Jacob recognized the robe.
Jacob said, “This is my son’s robe.”
Jacob said, “A wild animal has eaten him.”
Jacob said, “Joseph has been torn to pieces.”
passages.original: וַיַּכִּירָ֤הּ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ כְּתֹ֣נֶת בְּנִ֔י חַיָּ֥ה רָעָ֖ה אֲכָלָ֑תְהוּ טָרֹ֥ף טֹרַ֖ף יוֹסֵֽף׃

passages.text: Then Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned for his son many days.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of Joseph.
Jacob heard that Joseph was dead.
Jacob tore his clothes.
Jacob put sackcloth around his waist.
Jacob mourned for his son.
Jacob mourned for many days.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרַ֤ע יַעֲקֹב֙ שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם שַׂ֖ק בְּמָתְנָ֑יו וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֥ל עַל־ בְּנ֖וֹ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: All his sons and daughters tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said. “I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son.” So his father wept for him.
passages.sermon:
Jacob was the father of Joseph.
Jacob believed Joseph was dead.
All of Jacob’s sons tried to comfort him.
All of Jacob’s daughters tried to comfort him.
Jacob refused to be comforted.
Jacob said he would go down to Sheol mourning for his son.
Jacob’s father wept for him.
passages.original: וַיָּקֻמוּ֩ כָל־ בָּנָ֨יו וְכָל־ בְּנֹתָ֜יו לְנַחֲמ֗וֹ וַיְמָאֵן֙ לְהִתְנַחֵ֔ם וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כִּֽי־ אֵרֵ֧ד אֶל־ בְּנִ֛י אָבֵ֖ל שְׁאֹ֑לָה וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ אֹת֖וֹ אָבִֽיו׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.
passages.sermon:
The Midianites were traders.
They took Joseph to Egypt.
They sold Joseph in Egypt.
Potiphar bought Joseph.
Potiphar served Pharaoh.
Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh.
Potiphar was captain of the guard.
passages.original: וְהַ֨מְּדָנִ֔ים מָכְר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־ מִצְרָ֑יִם לְפֽוֹטִיפַר֙ סְרִ֣יס פַּרְעֹ֔ה שַׂ֖ר הַטַּבָּחִֽים׃פ
